clue.text: Head of state's opportunity with voting register from the East

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the East means reading right to left, so the register is turned round

parts.note: the electoral roll is the register of voters

explanation.surface: A head of state gets an opening thanks to a register of voters from eastern lands.
explanation.definitionFit: In Germany and Austria the head of government is called by this title, loosely a national leader.

clue.text: Hosts, and brags about diamonds

indicators.note: about means the bragging word goes around the diamonds letter

parts.note: to crow is to brag
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A host boasts about diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great multitude, as in a host of angels, so hosts are throngs.

clue.text: Experts change dates to absorb pressure

indicators.note: to absorb means the rearranged word takes the pressure letter inside
change tells us to rearrange the letters of dates

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Experts reschedule appointments to cope with pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a highly skilled person, so adepts are skilled practitioners.

clue.text: Organisations distributing food in centres across area

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters stretch over the area letter, holding it
distributing spreads the letters around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bodies hand out food at centres across a region.
explanation.definitionFit: A confederation is an alliance of states or groups, a kind of organisation.

clue.text: Lake poems with quality must be a magnet

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
odes are lyric poems
tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

explanation.surface: The Lake poets' verse has a quality that draws readers like a magnet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake Poets were Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey, who lived in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturally magnetised piece of iron ore, and figuratively anything that attracts.

clue.text: Houses where cooks go hatless?

indicators.note: going hatless loses the top, so the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to roast is to cook in an oven

explanation.surface: In which houses do chefs work without their hats?
explanation.walkthrough: Oasts are kilns for drying hops, typical of Kent; they are housed in oast houses.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a hop-drying kiln building, so oasts are a kind of farm house.

clue.text: Tax whisky, not the Church

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the church abbreviation out of the whisky word

parts.note: Scotch is whisky from Scotland
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A levy on whisky that the Church is spared.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a municipal levy, surviving in the phrase scot-free, meaning without paying.

clue.text: Obvious snub includes King Charles, initially

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch
to cut someone is to snub them

explanation.surface: An obvious snub to King Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' only says the snub piece takes in the other pieces in the run of letters; the order is C, LEAR, CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is plain and unambiguous, as in a clear-cut decision.

clue.text: Heart broken, with no energy, discarded and beaten

indicators.note: broken means the remaining letters are smashed and reassembled
with no means the energy letter is taken out

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to shed something is to discard it

explanation.surface: Heartbroken and drained of energy, someone is cast aside and defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes E out of HEART, leaving HART; 'broken' rearranges that to THRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thrashed is to be beaten soundly, whether in a fight or a match.

clue.text: Sun's taken on Left supporting magazine — there's something to watch

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: The Spectator is a British weekly magazine
S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A sun-tanned left-wing reader backs a magazine with something worth watching.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a long-running British political weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport such as football watched by crowds is one played for an audience.

clue.text: Indian, for example, once a drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something unsteady and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Indian man was once a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one of the world's great bodies of salt water, alongside the Atlantic and Pacific.

clue.text: Mostly peach — and a soft fruit — go missing

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a peach, informally an attractive person, is also a dish
P, for piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Most of a peach and a pear vanish from the fruit bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish or go missing is a straightforward synonym for ceasing to be seen.

clue.text: Hesitates — daughter is crossing the river

indicators.note: crossing means the word is stretches across the other pieces, which sit inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter hesitates before wading across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate, unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Guarantees European fix in Sevenoaks, disheartened

indicators.note: in places the European and fix pieces within the outer letters of the town
disheartened means the heart of the word is removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: to fix a problem is to cure it

explanation.surface: A European makes a repair in a Kent town that has lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Sevenoaks is a town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to guarantee or make it certain, as in securing a loan.

clue.text: Criminal case turned on deeply ingrained habit

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crime file reopened about someone with an ingrained habit of offending.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit practised so long that it feels instinctive, as if part of one's inborn character.

clue.text: Downhearted lower socioeconomic groups campaigned

parts.note: in British market research, D and E are the lowest social grades
to press for something is to campaign for it

explanation.surface: The poorest groups campaigned while feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK's NRS social grades run A, B, C1, C2, D and E, with D and E the lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressed and downhearted both describe a low, dispirited mood.

clue.text: Officially recognise deferred payment after bill

indicators.note: after places the payment word behind the bill abbreviation

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
buying on credit means paying later

explanation.surface: An institution recognises a payment deferred after a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit a body or person is to give official recognition or authorisation.

clue.text: Completely empty, but gave a cute play with no end of acting

indicators.note: play suggests letters moving freely, so they are rearranged
with no means the chosen letter is removed from the words
end of picks the last letter of the word acting

explanation.surface: A cute play by a cast who stopped acting empties the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of acting' gives G, which 'with no' removes from GAVE A CUTE, leaving AVEACUTE to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate a building is to clear it entirely of people.

clue.text: Commercial advice from chamber — a temporary worker to get rise

parts.note: a cave is an underground chamber
a temp is an office worker hired for a short stint
a tor is a rocky hill or rise, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A cave hires a temp who is set to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'let the buyer beware'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin maxim warns purchasers that they buy at their own risk, a piece of trading counsel.

clue.text: Craftsman getting delayed in Southern Region

indicators.note: in places the delay word inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: something delayed is late

explanation.surface: A craftsman is held up in the Southern Region.
explanation.walkthrough: Southern Region was a section of British Railways, notorious for late trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A slater is a tradesman who lays roofing slates.

clue.text: Bus not regularly on the way in Paris. That's not right!

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way in Paris

explanation.surface: A Paris bus not keeping to its route regularly is wrong!
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is false, so not correct.

clue.text: The repercussions of being fired?

parts.note: sounds like the aftermath of losing one's job, but means the kick a gun gives when shot

explanation.definitionFit: When a gun is fired it jerks backwards, so its kick-backs are literally what follows the shot.

clue.text: Vessel mostly loaded with American food for Japan

indicators.note: loaded with means the shortened vessel takes the American letters inside
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a ship is a sea vessel

explanation.surface: A ship mostly laden with American food bound for Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegared rice with raw fish is a classic Japanese dish.

clue.text: A letter in retinol is perfectly reversed

indicators.note: reversed says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A letter claims a vitamin cream works perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth character of the Greek alphabet, so one letter among many.

clue.text: Problem identification is doing as badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diagnosis is going badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's finding of what is wrong is the identification of a medical problem.

clue.text: External computer device with no lead

indicators.note: with no lead means the first letter is removed, a pun on a cable lead

parts.note: a router is a networking device connecting computers to the internet

explanation.surface: An external computer gadget comes without a cable.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer and external both describe what lies on the outside.

clue.text: Bound to get clocked, with minutes deducted

indicators.note: deducted says the minutes letter is taken away

parts.note: to be clocked is to be timed with a stopwatch

explanation.surface: Someone bound to be clocked, with minutes taken off the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bound with rope or string is tied up.

clue.text: Frenchman welcoming escort's bijou accommodation

indicators.note: welcoming means the Frenchman's name takes the escort inside it

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a date is someone who escorts you for an evening

explanation.surface: A Frenchman invites his escort into his small flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small second home kept in a town, a compact pad, so bijou lodgings.
